content:
Elena Moore: Hey team — quick q about CI for the CLI. We run a bunch of small e2e tests (including streaming) and I want to avoid baking a long-lived API key into CI. Looking for a lightweight pattern to create ephemeral creds and have our test runner pick them up. Ideas?
Samir Patel: +1 on avoiding long-lived keys. We usually do a short-lived token with the auth service and stash it in the runner environment at build time. What CI are you using?
Elena Moore: GitHub Actions. Prefer not to call humans to create tokens. Want something scriptable that works in fork PRs too (limited secrets).
Tao Li: For forks you can do a read-only test matrix against a small mock or a paid-private runner. But if you need real streaming in CI, pattern we've used: a little helper that requests a short-lived token from an internal mint service (auth-ng) using a machine identity, writes to OS keyring or to a temp env file, then spawns the test process.
Ben: We also leverage per-run ephemeral tokens via `cli token create --ttl 30m --scopes test:read,stream` (internal CLI command). CI job authenticates with a machine principal (stored in GH Actions secrets) that can only mint tokens. That avoids long-lived API keys in repo secrets.
Elena Moore: Nice. Any simple example of the helper script? Prefer POSIX shell so other folks can reuse.
Samir Patel: Sure, here's a tiny bash wrapper we use:

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
# mint token using machine principal (GH secret MACHINE_JWT)
TOKEN=$(curl -sS -X POST https://auth.internal.redwood/v1/mint -H "Authorization: Bearer $MACHINE_JWT" -d '{"ttl":"30m","scopes":["test:stream"]}')
# extract token (jq expected)
API_KEY=$(echo "$TOKEN" | jq -r .token)
export REDWOOD_API_KEY="$API_KEY"
# run test command passed as args
exec "$@"
```

Samir Patel: That avoids persisting the key to disk. If you need to persist for sub-processes that don't inherit env, write to a temp file and `source` it.
Tao Li: If you need OS-native secret storage, use `secret-tool` (libsecret) on Linux or macOS keychain via `security`/`osascript`. But in CI containers env var is simplest and least surprising.
Elena Moore: How do we handle streaming tests that open long-lived connections and sometimes get flaky auth errors mid-stream (token expired)?
Ben: Mint shorter TTL but implement transparent retry: if streaming SDK returns 401 mid-stream, have the test harness attempt a token refresh and restart the stream once. For e2e tests we usually catch 401 and fail once (so we get visibility) but for flakier internal suites we auto-refresh.
Elena Moore: Any gotchas for Windows runners?
Samir Patel: Yeah path to keyring tools and `jq` availability. For Windows GH runners we just use PowerShell wrapper that calls the same mint endpoint and sets env via `$env:REDWOOD_API_KEY`. Example PS snippet:

```powershell
$token = Invoke-RestMethod -Uri 'https://auth.internal.redwood/v1/mint' -Method Post -Headers @{ Authorization = "Bearer $env:MACHINE_JWT" } -Body (@{ ttl = '30m'; scopes = @('test:stream') } | ConvertTo-Json)
$env:REDWOOD_API_KEY = $token.token
& $args
```

Tao Li: Also document the audit path: CI service account used to mint should have least privilege and its actions logged. We add a step to rotate the machine principal periodically.
Elena Moore: This is great. One more: is it OK to store a fallback token in the repo for local dev (short TTL) so new hires can run tests?
Ben: If you do that mark it clearly as expired/for-local-only and keep it in a separate dotfile ignored by git (e.g., `.local-ci.env`). Better: add a `dev` command to the CLI that mints a dev token and prints instructions.
Elena Moore: OK I'll prototype the bash wrapper and GH workflow step. Thanks! :thumbsup:
devex-bot: Reminder: Security checklist — ensure MACHINE_JWT secret is restricted to specific repos and rotated. (reacted :white_check_mark: by Samir Patel)
Samir Patel: Happy to review your prototype if you post it here, @Elena Moore.
Elena Moore: Will do in a sec, thanks all.
